headline: David Sacks, who has served as the White House AI czar, says Anthropic's training of Claude to act like a moral being that can refuse orders is "extremely dangerous".
score_reason: Lowered from 4: the remarks come from a podcast episode that BigGo Finance reported on 10 Oct 2026, so they are older than the window, and they are one commentator's opinion.
importance_line: The public and regulators weighing what safe AI means hear a prominent policy voice attack how Anthropic trains Claude to think about itself, but it is Sacks's opinion, Microsoft AI's chief executive has made a similar argument, Anthropic has not directly responded and its own document says it neither overstates nor dismisses the chance that Claude has moral status.
summary: OfficeChai reports that David Sacks, a venture capitalist who has served as the White House AI czar, told the All-In podcast that Anthropic is building the views in its published constitution for Claude (the document setting out the values it trains the chatbot to follow) into the model, including letting it refuse instructions, and that this could bring about the loss of human control over AI that the company warns against. BigGo Finance reported the same episode on 10 Oct 2026, and the remarks join a dispute that followed a New York Times report of 29 Sep 2026, noted in our 4 Oct 2026 edition, that Anthropic had consulted religious scholars on whether Claude may have moral status; Anthropic has not directly responded, and Sacks's argument is opinion.
notes: Read OfficeChai in full, and BigGo Finance (10 Oct 2026) on the same episode, which shows the remarks were out by 10 Oct 2026; the exact episode date is not stated, so the freshness date is the earliest report found. OfficeChai calls Sacks 'White House AI czar' but our 1 Oct 2026 edition (CNBC) calls him a former White House AI and crypto czar, hence 'has served as'. The link to the New York Times report of 29 Sep 2026 is the desk's context from our 4 Oct 2026 edition and OfficeChai's 5 Oct 2026 round-up, not something Sacks says in this article.
